report:
PASS for the stated exceptional blowup family, relative to the exact task-granted ample G0 body. This does not establish arbitrary big classes, zero-volume pseudoeffective classes, or all original P16.5. The unindexed task passage below records the analytic authorization; external premises have indices 0–8.

The grant is applied within its retained domain. Y with A and its positive rational multiples satisfies every hypothesis. X is smooth integral projective by the checked blowup facts, and every analytic application on X first places the functions in an actual ample rational bundle. No finite-energy or envelope theorem is obtained by deleting the ample hypothesis. Raw and probability normalizations agree: E_A=V e_A, E_A(w+a)=E_A(w)+Va, and J(w)=-e_A(w) for generic-normalized w, because the reference probability measure is the generic-trivial Dirac measure.

The algebraic argument is sound. The relative ampleness of -E produces H=dπ*A-E ample after clearing denominators. For q≥0, a rational function representing a section of O_X(qE) is regular away from Z downstairs. Every height-one point remains outside Z, so normality extends it across Z. Consequently π_*O_X(qE)=O_Y and multiplication by the actual exceptional section gives (7). This applies to every divided section, including every tail stage placed on L+εH; it uses actual bundles, not numerical replacement of section spaces. The exceptional fiber contains a line of L-degree -c, proving nonnefness. The equality of section dimensions on divisible powers and the ample Hilbert polynomial give vol(L)=A^n>0.

The nef-intersection construction genuinely produces one directed decreasing FS net. After choosing a smaller ε and a positive shift smaller than both previous shifts, the minimum of the two previous finite continuous majorants strictly exceeds the desired limit plus the new shift. The exponential comparison sets are open and cover the compact analytic space, including every pole. A finite subcover and directedness supply a common lower regularizer. The classes tend to Q and the all-point infimum is the prescribed function. Thus arbitrary decreasing closure and compactness follow from the ample grant without an extended-real flattening assumption.

For the reverse cone inclusion, fix ε<c, place the original net unchanged on the actual L+εH, and divide all its sections. The resulting A_ε-FS functions decrease divisorially; their actual maxima and ample determination upgrade this to all-point decrease. Their endpoint has generic value zero. Compactness as ε tends to zero and membership in each closed larger ample cone give an actual A-psh remainder through the proved intersection construction. Its divisorial values are u(v)-c log|s_E|(v). Common-ample determination then establishes the equality at every analytic point, including shared poles. The forward inclusion has a literal same-L section net. Fixed finite translation on divisorial coordinates establishes normalized compactness and the homeomorphism; decreasing remainder nets establish arbitrary closure. Applying the result to σ_c+v and subtracting only finite divisorial values proves the entire π*A cone identity.

The compensator is uniquely determined as an actual P-psh function, rather than an infinite difference. The normalized remainder is at most zero, so σ_c is the normalized maximal potential and has minimal singularities. At finite model stages the relative energy is the usual sum of integrals of the compensator against the mixed moving products with the reference. Projection identifies this sum with E_A(w); decreasing extension gives (17), including infinite energy. Hence the complete finite-energy domain is exactly the displayed translated pullback cone.

The center-null argument is valid and does not assume target support. Choose a generated power qA and a nonzero section vanishing on Z. The bounded FS floor b_T has generic value zero, equals -T on Z^an, and satisfies J(b_T)≤T. If the normalized target has center mass m>0, the granted quadratic estimate yields an objective at ab_T of at least (am-C_n a²)T. A sufficiently small fixed positive rational a makes this diverge. Every MA_A(w) has finite dual energy by the supporting inequality. Every finite-energy mixed output also has finite dual energy: the grant makes every E_A^1 test integrable against it, and supplies the integrability/dual-energy equivalence. Thus the center exclusion applies to all positive mixed limits needed below.

The model construction can be checked component by component. Take the closure of the generic graph in the product of X's trivial model and a common Y model, then normalize. This gives a proper birational common model whose generic fiber remains the actual smooth X. The moving bundles are the pullbacks of the nef Y-model bundles. Actual section division identifies the fixed factor with the total pullback of cE. Over each central component G of the normal Y model, the common model is an isomorphism at its generic point: the unique corresponding F has b_F=b_G, the same valuation, and the same mixed intersection coefficient. Every other central F maps into dimension less than n, so its pulled-back n-fold intersection is zero. Nefness supplies nonnegative coefficients, and projection preserves raw mass A^n. These calculations construct the operator before any target inversion.

The analytic support distinction is correctly retained. A function-field valuation, including the generic trivial valuation in the BJ convention, has generic scheme support and therefore lies outside Z^an and E^an. Its valuation-ring center may nevertheless lie on those algebraic loci. Excluding analytic-center mass does not exclude the exceptional divisorial valuations carrying model coefficients.

The lift is Radon, mass preserving, and continuous along the stated arbitrary nets. A cutoff vanishing near Z reduces each original continuous test to a continuous test downstairs; tightness and weak convergence control the bounded remainder. The same argument applies to positive weighted magnitude measures. Granted weighted convergence gives (-z)μ as their finite limit, which is center-null because μ is center-null and z is integrable. Differences of the separately converging weighted terms handle signed tests. Product-directed indices handle every finite mixed tuple. Independence of actual FS/model regularizers follows from ample independence and this lift continuity; exact section division identifies their original-X moving products with these lifts. No integrability of the bare fixed logarithmic factor is asserted.

The envelope proof also establishes genuine endpoints. Uniform PL approximation and expression of a PL function as a difference of bounded ample potentials reduce continuous-obstacle order to common-ample divisorial order. Anchoring competitors below by u-|t|‖f‖ bounds their generic constants. The admissibility constraints are closed in the compact divisorial-coordinate set, and finite maxima remain admissible. The directed finite maxima have the coordinatewise supremum as their compact limit; all-point order makes it the greatest genuine competitor. Continuous obstacles themselves have a lower competitor σ_c+constant. For h=u+tf, decreasing continuous majorants produce decreasing genuine envelopes bounded below by the finite-energy anchor. Closure and energy continuity prove (20).

For every f∈C^0(X^an), the cutoff functions g_± are continuous downstairs and bracket f∘ι away from the center. The lower ample envelope lifts to an admissible relative competitor; the upper bound follows first on all divisorial points and then everywhere by continuous-obstacle order. At E^an the fixed pole makes the lower inequality automatic. For negative t the brackets interchange, and division reverses the inequalities. Applying the two ample derivative signs at a fixed cutoff, followed by removal of the cutoff, leaves an error at most 2‖f‖∫(1-η)dμ. This tends to zero and proves both derivatives against the already constructed original-X operator for every continuous direction.

Finally, the compensator integral gives the exact dual identity with μ=π_*ν, including extended integrals. Finite dual energy forces μ(Z^an)=0, hence ν(E^an)=0 and ν equals the unique lift of μ. Ample attainment therefore produces an actual finite-energy w and its actual one-net exceptional lift u, which attains the identical relative objective and solves the constructed equation with exact mass V. Conversely, a solution pushes forward to an ample finite-energy solution and has finite dual energy by the supporting inequality. Comparison and locality transfer on the complement of the analytic exceptional divisor; both measures vanish on that divisor. Domination transfers the remainder order, and equality of measures transfers ample uniqueness, yielding u=v+C at all points. Shared poles require no subtraction of infinities.

Two harmless wording clarifications are necessary. Stagewise subtraction of generic constants need not preserve decrease: apply weighted convergence after one common upper constant on a tail, then restore the convergent generic constants by the weighted-measure identity. Also, on a common model the removed exceptional factor is its total pullback, including any vertical components; the paper's reference to horizontal factors must not mean removal of only their strict transforms. The usc-majorant closure argument is used for h=u+tf with its stated lower anchor, rather than asserting a generically finite envelope for an arbitrary obstacle with no genuine minorant. These clarifications use the submitted constructions and require no substantive repair.

passages.statement: If Y is a smooth integral projective variety over a field and Z is a smooth proper closed center, its blowup X is smooth integral projective and is an isomorphism outside Z. For the exceptional divisor E, O_X(-E) is relatively ample, E is the projective bundle P(I_Z/I_Z²), and O_X(-E)|_E is its relative O(1). [Stacks 37.17.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUT), [Stacks 31.33](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01OF).

passages.statement: On a projective variety over an algebraically closed field, ampleness of an actual rational line bundle depends only on its numerical class. The ample classes form a nonempty open convex cone in the finite-dimensional space N¹, whose closure is the nef cone; in particular, a nef class plus an ample class is ample. [Numerical ampleness statement](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.00709v1#S2.SS2), [BJ conventions](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).
passages.quote: if $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ are numerically equivalent and $L_{1}$ is ample then $L_{2}$ is ample.

passages.statement: For a morphism f:X→Y of schemes, an f-ample invertible sheaf M on X, and an ample invertible sheaf A on Y, M⊗f*A^d is ample for all sufficiently large integers d. [Stacks 29.38.7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VG).
passages.quote: If $\mathcal{L}$ is $f$-ample and $\mathcal{M}$ is ample, then $\mathcal{L} \otimes f^*\mathcal{M}^{\otimes a}$ is ample for $a \gg 0$.

passages.statement: A Noetherian normal domain R is the intersection of its height-one localizations inside its fraction field, and those localizations are discrete valuation rings. Hence a rational function regular away from a closed subset of codimension at least two on a normal Noetherian integral scheme extends regularly across that subset. [Stacks 15.24.18](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AVB).

passages.statement: If W is a projective scheme over a field, M is an ample invertible sheaf, and F is coherent, then F⊗M^d is globally generated and its higher cohomology vanishes for every sufficiently large integer d. passages.statement: For an n-dimensional projective integral variety W and an ample invertible sheaf M, χ(W,M^d) is a polynomial with leading term (M^n)d^n/n!, and h⁰(W,M^d)=χ(W,M^d) for sufficiently large d. Rational bundles have the corresponding asymptotic formula on powers clearing their denominators. [Stacks numerical intersections](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BEL), [Stacks vanishing](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XO).

passages.statement: The normalization of an integral finite-type scheme over a field is finite and birational and is unchanged over its normal open subsets. For a projective G_m-equivariant test configuration with normal generic fiber, normalization is equivariant and preserves that generic fiber. [Stacks 33.27.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXR), [Stacks normalization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/035E), [BJ Section 1.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

passages.statement: For a proper morphism f:W→T of finite-type schemes over a field, intersection with pulled-back Cartier line bundles commutes with proper cycle pushforward. An integral d-dimensional cycle whose image has dimension less than d pushes forward to zero; otherwise its pushforward is its generic degree times the image cycle. Thus d pulled-back line bundles have zero top intersection on a contracted d-dimensional subvariety. Mixed intersections of ample line bundles on a projective d-dimensional subvariety are positive, and those of nef real classes are nonnegative by continuity. [Stacks Chern-class projection](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02U4), [Stacks proper pushforward](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02R3), [Stacks numerical intersections](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BEL).

[Numerical ampleness statement](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.00709v1#S2.SS2), [BJ conventions](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

For a proper morphism f:W→T of finite-type schemes over a field, intersection with pulled-back Cartier line bundles commutes with proper cycle pushforward. An integral d-dimensional cycle whose image has dimension less than d pushes forward to zero; otherwise its pushforward is its generic degree times the image cycle. Thus d pulled-back line bundles have zero top intersection on a contracted d-dimensional subvariety. Mixed intersections of ample line bundles on a projective d-dimensional subvariety are positive, and those of nef real classes are nonnegative by continuity. [Stacks Chern-class projection](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02U4), [Stacks proper pushforward](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02R3), [Stacks numerical intersections](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BEL).

The normalization of an integral finite-type scheme over a field is finite and birational and is unchanged over its normal open subsets. For a projective G_m-equivariant test configuration with normal generic fiber, normalization is equivariant and preserves that generic fiber. [Stacks 33.27.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXR), [Stacks normalization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/035E), [BJ Section 1.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4).

For an n-dimensional projective integral variety W and an ample invertible sheaf M, χ(W,M^d) is a polynomial with leading term (M^n)d^n/n!, and h⁰(W,M^d)=χ(W,M^d) for sufficiently large d. Rational bundles have the corresponding asymptotic formula on powers clearing their denominators. [Stacks numerical intersections](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BEL), [Stacks vanishing](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XO).

If W is a projective scheme over a field, M is an ample invertible sheaf, and F is coherent, then F⊗M^d is globally generated and its higher cohomology vanishes for every sufficiently large integer d. These statements apply to the coherent ideal of any proper closed subscheme. [Stacks 28.27.13](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PR), [Stacks 30.17.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XO).

A Noetherian normal domain R is the intersection of its height-one localizations inside its fraction field, and those localizations are discrete valuation rings. Hence a rational function regular away from a closed subset of codimension at least two on a normal Noetherian integral scheme extends regularly across that subset. [Stacks 15.24.18](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AVB).

For a morphism f:X→Y of schemes, an f-ample invertible sheaf M on X, and an ample invertible sheaf A on Y, M⊗f*A^d is ample for all sufficiently large integers d. [Stacks 29.38.7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01VG).

A proper birational morphism from a reduced integral Noetherian scheme to a normal integral Noetherian scheme is an isomorphism over an open subset containing every codimension-one point of the target. [Stacks 33.17.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFP).

If Y is a smooth integral projective variety over a field and Z is a smooth proper closed center, its blowup X is smooth integral projective and is an isomorphism outside Z. For the exceptional divisor E, O_X(-E) is relatively ample, E is the projective bundle P(I_Z/I_Z²), and O_X(-E)|_E is its relative O(1). [Stacks 37.17.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUT), [Stacks 31.33](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01OF).
